title: Choosing the Right Carrier Size for Your Dog
excerpt: A wobbly, too-small carrier is uncomfortable and an oversized one can feel unsettling. Here's how to measure your dog properly before you buy.
content:
Getting the size right matters more than almost anything else when choosing a carrier. Too small and your dog can't turn around comfortably. Too large and they may feel less secure, since most dogs prefer a snug, den-like space rather than a lot of open room around them.

## How to Measure Your Dog Properly

Start by measuring your dog from nose to tail base for length, then from the floor to the top of their head or ears (whichever is taller) for height, and across their shoulders for width. Add a few centimetres to each measurement for comfortable movement, but avoid adding too much extra space, since a carrier that's too roomy can leave a dog feeling unsteady rather than secure once it's moving.

If your dog is between sizes, we'd usually suggest sizing up slightly for longer journeys and keeping it snugger for short trips, since a close fit helps many dogs feel calmer when the carrier is in motion.

## Weight Limits Matter Just as Much as Dimensions

Every carrier on our site lists a maximum recommended weight, and it's worth checking this even if your dog looks like they'd fit by size alone, since the base and handles need to support them safely. A carrier can look roomy enough on paper while still being under-built for a heavier dog's actual weight.

## Matching Size to the Right Category

Once you know your dog's measurements and weight, it's usually quicker to shop within the size band that fits rather than browsing everything. Our [small dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers) range covers dogs up to around 10kg, [medium dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/medium-dog-carriers) covers roughly 10kg to 25kg, and [large dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/large-dog-carriers) is built for dogs heavier than that, with a sturdier frame to match.

## If Your Dog Is Still a Puppy

A young puppy who hasn't reached their adult size yet is usually better served by a carrier sized to where they are now rather than where they'll end up. Our [puppy carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers) range is built specifically around that smaller, still-growing stage, and you can move up to an adult size once they're closer to their full weight. For the full range organised by both size and format, our [dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers) hub is worth a browse too.

title: Helping a Nervous Cat Get Used to a Carrier
excerpt: Most cats associate the carrier with the vet and little else. A bit of patience beforehand can make a real difference.
content:
Cats tend to link the carrier with one thing: the vet. That association alone can make getting them inside a battle every single time. The good news is that a little groundwork between trips can change how your cat feels about it.

## Why Cats React This Way

Most cats only see their carrier a handful of times a year, almost always right before an unfamiliar, slightly stressful trip. Without more regular, low-stakes exposure, the carrier itself becomes a signal that something unsettling is about to happen, rather than just another object in the house.

## Getting the Carrier Ready Before Travel Day

Leave the carrier out in a quiet corner of the house for a week or two before you need to use it, ideally with a soft blanket inside and maybe a few treats scattered near the entrance. Let your cat investigate in their own time rather than pushing them towards it. Repeating this every so often, not just before a trip, helps break the association with stress specifically.

## Choosing a Carrier That Helps Rather Than Hinders

When it's time to travel, a carrier with a top-loading opening tends to cause far less stress than one with only a front door, since you can lower your cat in gently rather than having to push them through a narrow gap. Our [cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers) range is built with exactly this kind of calmer, more enclosed handling in mind, and our [soft-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) range is a good starting point if your cat hasn't had a carrier before.

## On the Day of Travel

Covering part of the carrier with a light cloth during the journey can also help, as it reduces visual stimulation and gives your cat a smaller, calmer space to settle into. Keep handling brief and matter-of-fact rather than making a fuss, since cats often pick up on an owner's own tension around the carrier.

## If a Vet Visit Is What's Bringing You Here

If it's specifically an upcoming vet appointment prompting this, our [pet carriers for vet visits](/carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits) range picks out designs suited to that shorter, more clinical kind of trip across every pet we carry, not just cats.

title: Flying with Your Pet: What UK Airlines Expect
excerpt: Cabin carrier rules vary a great deal between airlines. Here's what to check before you book.
content:
If you're planning to fly with a small pet, the carrier you choose matters just as much as the ticket you book. Most UK airlines that allow pets in the cabin set their own maximum carrier dimensions and combined pet-and-carrier weight limits, and these can differ quite a bit from one airline to the next.

## What Most Airlines Look For

As a general rule, look for a soft-sided carrier that can compress slightly to fit under the seat in front of you, with mesh panelling for airflow during the flight. Rigid carriers are rarely accepted in the cabin, though they may be suitable for hold travel with the right preparation. A secure, lockable zip matters too, since airport handling is busy and a closure that can't be fixed shut is a genuine risk during boarding.

## Always Confirm With Your Airline First

Always confirm pet travel rules directly with your airline before booking, ideally at the time of booking rather than afterwards, since space for pets in the cabin is usually limited and allocated on a first-come basis. We're not able to guarantee that any carrier meets a specific airline's requirements, so please check the current published guidelines for your airline before you travel.

## Choosing the Right Carrier for Cabin Travel

Our [airline approved pet carriers](/carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers) range covers cabin-friendly designs across every pet type, with sizing built around the kind of low, flat profile most airlines expect. For dogs and cats specifically, our [airline approved dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/airline-approved-dog-carriers) and [airline approved cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/airline-approved-cat-carriers) ranges are sized around each animal's typical proportions rather than being a one-size-fits-all design.

## Beyond the Flight Itself

Don't forget the journey to and from the airport too. If you're driving, our [pet carriers for car travel](/carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers) range covers carriers built to stay stable and properly secured on the back seat or in the boot, which matters just as much as the cabin-approved carrier itself once you're actually on the road.

title: Settling a Rabbit or Guinea Pig for a Short Trip
excerpt: Small pets can find travel unsettling. A few small changes to how you prepare can help them stay calmer.
content:
Rabbits and guinea pigs are creatures of routine, so any change, including travel, can be unsettling if you don't prepare a little in advance. The good news is that small adjustments can make a noticeable difference.

## Why Small Pets Find Travel Harder

Unlike dogs and cats, rabbits and guinea pigs rarely leave home, so a carrier journey is often a genuinely new experience each time rather than something they've built up any tolerance for. Their instinct when unsettled is usually to freeze or brace against the ground, which is why the carrier itself matters so much here.

## Preparing the Carrier Before You Leave

Line the base of the carrier with familiar bedding from their usual home, along with a small handful of hay, so the space smells reassuringly like home rather than new and unfamiliar. Avoid cleaning the carrier too thoroughly right before travel for the same reason.

## Choosing a Carrier Built for the Right Pet

A solid, non-slip base matters more here than for almost any other pet, since rabbits and guinea pigs need something to grip rather than a mesh floor to sit on. Our [small animal carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers) range covers this properly, and our [rabbit carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/rabbit-carriers) and [guinea pig carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/guinea-pig-carriers) ranges are each sized and shaped around their different builds.

## Keeping the Journey Calm

Keep the journey as smooth and quiet as you reasonably can. Sudden stops, loud music or a lot of handling along the way tend to raise stress levels more than the travel itself. For longer trips, check whether your pet may need access to water or extra ventilation, and always keep the carrier out of direct sunlight in a warm car.

title: Soft-Sided vs Hard-Shell Carriers: Which Is Right for You?
excerpt: Both styles have their place. Here's how to decide which suits your pet, your journeys and your storage space.
content:
Soft-sided and hard-shell carriers each suit different situations, and there's rarely a single right answer, only a better fit for how you actually travel.

## The Core Trade-Off

Soft-sided carriers are lighter, fold flat for storage and tend to feel less clinical to a nervous pet, since the fabric gives slightly and the shape is less rigid. Hard-shell carriers offer more protection on longer car journeys or when checked as hold luggage, since the rigid shell resists knocks that a soft carrier simply couldn't. Neither is objectively better, it depends on how often you'll use it and what you'll be doing with it.

## When Soft-Sided Makes Sense

They're usually the better choice for short, everyday trips such as the vet or a quick visit to family, where light weight and easy storage matter more than maximum rigidity. Our [soft-sided pet carriers](/carriers/pet-soft-sided-carriers) range covers this construction across every pet we sell.

## When Hard-Shell Makes Sense

Hard-shell carriers are also easier to disinfect thoroughly, which matters if you're bringing a new pet home or dealing with an unwell one, and they hold their shape better when stacked with other luggage or handled by a pet prone to pawing at the sides. Our [hard-sided pet carriers](/carriers/pet-hard-sided-carriers) range covers that sturdier construction instead.

## What About Specific Pets?

If you're shopping specifically for a cat, our [soft-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) and [hard-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-carriers) ranges cover the same trade-off sized around a cat's typical proportions rather than a general-purpose design.

## Making the Decision

If you're only ever making short trips nearby, a soft carrier will usually serve you well. If you travel further afield more often, or your pet needs a bit more structure and protection, it may be worth having a hard-shell option too.
